ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows triangle QPR, with a right-angle mark at vertex P. Side QP is labeled 37, side QR is labeled 58, and the problem asks for the measure of ∠R. Reasoning: Because P is a right angle, QR, which is opposite the right angle, is the hypotenuse, with length 58. For angle R, its opposite side is QP, with length 37. Therefore use the sine ratio: sin(R) = 37/58. Calculate R = arcsin(37/58) ≈ 39.6°, rounded to the nearest tenth as 39.6°.

raw_record.question_text: Find the measure of $\angle R$ to the nearest tenth.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: triangle QPR has a right-angle marker at P, side QP is labeled 37, and side QR is labeled 58; since QR is opposite the right angle, it is the hypotenuse. The text asks for the measure of angle R to the nearest tenth. Use the sine ratio for angle R: the side opposite angle R is QP = 37 and the hypotenuse is QR = 58, so sin(R) = 37/58. Compute R = arcsin(37/58) and round to the nearest tenth, giving 39.6 degrees.
